scenes.title: Attention, per head — tfQh, tfKh, tfVh, tfAttnH, tfHeadOut, tfConcat, tfAttnOut
scenes.description: One layer of attention with every head exposed: pick the head, change the head count or share K/V, and read each function's lattice.
scenes.markdown:
This lesson is a **function tour** of the transformer domain library, not a lesson about transformers: every lattice is labelled with the call that fills it, so an author can see what each function returns and how the `tf_*` sliders reshape it. The weights are the hand-built toy at layer 0 / head 0 and **seeded tables everywhere else — nothing here is learned.**

## Attention, per head

Head $h$ reads K/V head $g=\left\lfloor h\,n_{kv}/n_{heads}\right\rfloor$ — that is `tfHeadKv(h)`. $X$ below is the input stream.

**`tfH(0, i, d)`** · n × d_model · the input stream, one row per slot
$$X_{id}$$

**`tfWq(l, h, r, c)`**, **`tfWk(l, g, r, c)`**, **`tfWv(l, g, r, c)`** · d_model × d_k
$$\bigl(W_Q^{(l,h)}\bigr)_{rc},\qquad \bigl(W_K^{(l,g)}\bigr)_{rc},\qquad \bigl(W_V^{(l,g)}\bigr)_{rc}$$

**`tfQh(l, h, i, d)`** · n × d_k · rotated by RoPE when `s2_rope` is on
$$q_{id}=\sum_{r}X_{ir}\bigl(W_Q^{(h)}\bigr)_{rd}$$

**`tfKh(l, h, i, d)`** · n × d_k · shared by every head with the same $g$
$$k_{id}=\sum_{r}X_{ir}\bigl(W_K^{(g)}\bigr)_{rd}$$

**`tfVh(l, h, i, d)`** · n × d_k · **never** rotated by RoPE
$$v_{id}=\sum_{r}X_{ir}\bigl(W_V^{(g)}\bigr)_{rd}$$

**`tfScoreH(l, h, i, j)`** · n × n · raw, unscaled, unmasked
$$S_{ij}=q_i\cdot k_j$$

**`tfScoreScaledH(l, h, i, j)`** · n × n · $s$ is the **divisor** slider
$$\tilde S_{ij}=\frac{S_{ij}}{\bigl(\sqrt{d_k}\bigr)^{s}}$$

**`tfAttnH(l, h, i, j)`** · n × n · additive mask, **before** the softmax, so rows sum to 1
$$A_{ij}=\operatorname{softmax}_j\bigl(\tilde S_{ij}+m_{ij}\bigr)$$
$$m_{ij}=\begin{cases}0 & j\le i\\ -10^{9} & j>i\end{cases}$$

**`tfHeadOut(l, h, i, d)`** · n × d_k · head $h$'s output, before $W_O$
$$O^{(h)}_{id}=\sum_{j}A_{ij}\,v_{jd}$$

**`tfConcat(l, i, c)`** · n × n_heads·d_k · column $c$ belongs to head $\lfloor c/d_k\rfloor$
$$C_{i,\;h d_k+d}=O^{(h)}_{id}$$

**`tfWo(l, r, c)`** · n_heads·d_k × d_model · the projection back to $d_{model}$
$$\bigl(W_O^{(l)}\bigr)_{rc}$$

**`tfAttnOut(l, i, d)`** · n × d_model · the increment attention adds to the stream
$$\bigl(C\,W_O\bigr)_{id}$$

Drag **head shown** to switch heads; **tf_heads** to 4 gives four heads of d_k = 1 (the concat stays 4 wide); **tf_kv** to 1 makes every head read the same K and V. The head count starts at 2 here because the lattices are drawn two head-dimensions wide: one head would mean d_k = 4, and its q, k and v would not fit. $W_O$ is a tensor slider bound to its lattice: hover a cell to edit it.

## The arithmetic

Query head $h$ reads K/V head $g=\lfloor h\,n_{kv}/n_{heads}\rfloor$ (`tfHeadKv(h)`), so with $X$ the stream `tfH(0, i, d)`:

$$Q = X\,W_Q^{(h)},\qquad K = X\,W_K^{(g)},\qquad V = X\,W_V^{(g)}\qquad (n\times d_k)$$

$$S_{ij}=q_i\cdot k_j,\qquad \tilde S_{ij}=\frac{S_{ij}}{\left(\sqrt{d_k}\right)^{s}}$$

$s$ is the **divisor** slider: $s=0$ divides by $1$, $s=1$ by $\sqrt{d_k}$, and the values between are the interpolation you can drag through.

$$A_{ij}=\operatorname{softmax}_j\!\left(\tilde S_{ij}+m_{ij}\right),\qquad m_{ij}=\begin{cases}0 & j\le i\\[2pt] -10^{9} & j>i\end{cases}$$

The mask is **additive and applied before the softmax**, so every row of `tfAttnH` sums to exactly 1. (Masking after the softmax, by zeroing the future, leaves rows that do not sum to 1 — that is a misconception beat elsewhere, not reachable here.)

$$O^{(h)}_{id}=\sum_{j} A_{ij}\,v_{jd},\qquad \operatorname{concat}_{i,\;h\,d_k+d}=O^{(h)}_{id},\qquad \texttt{tfAttnOut} = \operatorname{concat}\,W_O$$

so column $c$ of `tfConcat` belongs to head $\lfloor c/d_k\rfloor$, and $W_O$ is $n_{heads}d_k\times d_{model}$.

**Each query row is computed on its own.** Row $i$ depends on $q_i$ and on *all* of $k_j,v_j$ — and on no other query. That is why **query slot to follow** moves the two charts and leaves every lattice still: it selects a row of a table that is already complete. It is also why $K$ and $V$ are worth caching, and why all $n$ queries are one matmul rather than a loop.

scenes.title: The block — tfAttnIn, tfResid1, tfFfIn, tfFfPre, tfFfHidden, tfFfOut, tfResid2
scenes.description: The residual stream through one layer: attention increment, FFN increment, and where the norms sit.
scenes.markdown:
This lesson is a **function tour** of the transformer domain library, not a lesson about transformers: every lattice is labelled with the call that fills it, so an author can see what each function returns and how the `tf_*` sliders reshape it. The weights are the hand-built toy at layer 0 / head 0 and **seeded tables everywhere else — nothing here is learned.**

## The block

$h^{(l)}$ is the stream entering layer $l$, $N$ the normalisation in force, and $\phi$ the activation. Each entry gives pre-norm first, post-norm after the semicolon where they differ.

**`tfH(l, i, d)`** · stream entering layer $l$
$$h^{(l)}_{id}$$

**`tfAttnIn(l, i, d)`** · what attention reads
$$a=N\!\left(h^{(l)}\right);\qquad a=h^{(l)}$$

**`tfAttnOut(l, i, d)`** · the attention increment
$$\operatorname{Attn}(a)_{id}$$

**`tfResid1(l, i, d)`** · after the first residual add
$$r_1=h^{(l)}+\operatorname{Attn}(a);\qquad r_1=N\!\left(h^{(l)}+\operatorname{Attn}(a)\right)$$

**`tfFfIn(l, i, d)`** · what the FFN reads
$$f=N(r_1);\qquad f=r_1$$

**`tfW1(l, r, c)`**, **`tfW2(l, r, c)`** · d_model × d_ff, then d_ff × d_model
$$\bigl(W_1^{(l)}\bigr)_{rc},\qquad \bigl(W_2^{(l)}\bigr)_{rc}$$

**`tfFfPre(l, i, k)`** · hidden units before the activation
$$u_{ik}=\bigl(f\,W_1\bigr)_{ik}$$

**`tfFfHidden(l, i, k)`** · after it — SwiGLU is the exception, see below
$$\phi(u_{ik})$$

**`tfFfOut(l, i, d)`** · the FFN increment
$$\bigl(\phi(u)\,W_2\bigr)_{id}$$

**`tfResid2(l, i, d)`** · stream leaving layer $l$, and equal to `tfH(l+1)`
$$r_2=r_1+\operatorname{FFN}(f);\qquad r_2=N\!\left(r_1+\operatorname{FFN}(f)\right)$$

Switch **tf_norm** between none, LayerNorm and RMSNorm and **tf_prenorm** between pre and post; the card checks the residual identity and the row mean live. **tf_act** changes what happens between `tfFfPre` and `tfFfHidden`.

## The arithmetic

With $h$ the stream entering the layer and $N$ the normalisation in force:

$$\textbf{pre-norm}\quad a=N(h),\quad r_1=h+\operatorname{Attn}(a),\quad f=N(r_1),\quad r_2=r_1+\operatorname{FFN}(f)$$

$$\textbf{post-norm}\quad a=h,\quad r_1=N\!\left(h+\operatorname{Attn}(h)\right),\quad f=r_1,\quad r_2=N\!\left(r_1+\operatorname{FFN}(r_1)\right)$$

Pre-norm normalises what a sub-layer *reads* and adds its raw output, so $r_2-h-\texttt{tfAttnOut}-\texttt{tfFfOut}=0$ identically — the card checks exactly that. Post-norm normalises the *sum*, so the identity does not hold.

Row by row, with unit gain and zero bias:

$$N(x)_d=\frac{x_d-\mu}{\sqrt{\sigma^2+\varepsilon}},\qquad \mu=\frac{1}{d_{model}}\sum_k x_k,\qquad \sigma^2=\frac{1}{d_{model}}\sum_k (x_k-\mu)^2$$

**RMSNorm is the same expression with $\mu=0$** — no mean subtraction and no bias. That is the whole difference, and it is why the card's row mean of `tfAttnIn` is zero under LayerNorm and not under RMSNorm.

The FFN widens to $d_{ff}$ and comes back:

$$\texttt{tfFfPre}=f\,W_1,\qquad \texttt{tfFfHidden}=\phi\!\left(\texttt{tfFfPre}\right),\qquad \texttt{tfFfOut}=\texttt{tfFfHidden}\,W_2$$

$$\phi_{\text{ReLU}}(z)=\max(0,z),\qquad \phi_{\text{GELU}}(z)=\tfrac12 z\left(1+\tanh\!\left[\sqrt{2/\pi}\left(z+0.044715\,z^{3}\right)\right]\right)$$

**SwiGLU is the exception: it is not elementwise.** It needs a second matrix $W_3$ of the same shape as $W_1$, and multiplies two projections of the same input together:

$$\texttt{tfFfHidden}=\operatorname{SiLU}\!\left(f W_1\right)\odot\left(f W_3\right),\qquad \operatorname{SiLU}(z)=\frac{z}{1+e^{-z}}$$

so under `tf_act` = SwiGLU the before/after chart is no longer a function of the orange point alone — the gate is a second, unplotted quantity.

scenes.title: Stack and sample — tfH by depth, tfFinal, tfWu, tfLogit, tfProb, tfArgmax, tfEntropy
scenes.description: The stream at every depth, the unembedding, and the next-token distribution under temperature.
scenes.markdown:
This lesson is a **function tour** of the transformer domain library, not a lesson about transformers: every lattice is labelled with the call that fills it, so an author can see what each function returns and how the `tf_*` sliders reshape it. The weights are the hand-built toy at layer 0 / head 0 and **seeded tables everywhere else — nothing here is learned.**

## Stack and sample

$L=$ `tf_layers`, so $h^{(L)}$ is the stream leaving the last block. $|V|$ is the vocabulary size.

**`tfH(l, i, d)`** for l = 0 … tf_layers · $L+1$ states for $L$ blocks
$$h^{(l)}_{id}$$

**`tfFinal(i, d)`** · what the unembedding reads
$$N\!\left(h^{(L)}\right)_{id}\ \ \text{under pre-norm};\qquad h^{(L)}_{id}\ \ \text{otherwise}$$

**`tfWu(v, d)`** · **tied**: row $v$ *is* word $v$'s embedding row, not a separate matrix
$$\bigl(W_U\bigr)_{vd}=E_{vd}$$

**`tfLogit(i, v)`** · a similarity between slot $i$ and word $v$
$$z_{iv}=\sum_{d}\text{final}_{id}\,\bigl(W_U\bigr)_{vd}$$

**`tfProb(i, v)`** · $T=$ `tf_temp` divides the logits inside the softmax and nowhere else
$$p_{iv}=\operatorname{softmax}_v\!\left(\frac{z_{iv}}{T}\right)$$

**`tfArgmax(i)`**, **`tfVocabToken(v)`** · taken on the **logits**, so $T$ cannot move it
$$\arg\max_v z_{iv}$$

**`tfEntropy(i)`** · in bits, with $0\le H_i\le\log_2\lvert V\rvert$
$$H_i=-\sum_{v}p_{iv}\log_2 p_{iv}$$

Drag **tf_temp** towards 0.05 and every row of `tfProb` collapses onto its argmax; towards 5 and it flattens to 0.2 each. Add layers with **tf_layers** and watch the stream drift with depth.

## The arithmetic

With $h_L$ the stream leaving the last layer ($L=$ `tf_layers`):

$$\texttt{tfFinal}=\begin{cases}N(h_L) & \text{pre-norm, with a norm on}\\[2pt] h_L & \text{otherwise}\end{cases}$$

The unembedding is **tied**: row $v$ of $W_U$ *is* the embedding row of word $v$, not a separate learned matrix. So a logit is a dot product between the final stream and a word's own embedding — a similarity, literally:

$$\texttt{tfLogit}(i,v)=\texttt{tfFinal}_{i\cdot}\cdot W_U^{(v)}=\sum_{d}\texttt{tfFinal}(i,d)\,\texttt{tfWu}(v,d)$$

$$\texttt{tfProb}(i,v)=\operatorname{softmax}_v\!\left(\frac{\texttt{tfLogit}(i,v)}{T}\right),\qquad T=\texttt{tf\_temp}$$

**Temperature divides the logits inside the softmax and nowhere else** — `tfLogit` is untouched by it. That is why dragging `tf_temp` moves the probability chart while the logit chart holds perfectly still. As $T\to 0$ the softmax tends to a one-hot on the argmax; as $T$ grows it tends to the uniform $1/|V|$.

$$\texttt{tfArgmax}(i)=\arg\max_v \texttt{tfLogit}(i,v),\qquad \texttt{tfEntropy}(i)=-\sum_v p_{iv}\log_2 p_{iv}\ \ \text{bits}$$

Entropy is bounded by $0\le H\le \log_2|V|$, so with a vocabulary of $|V|$ words the flat distribution sits at $\log_2|V|$ bits and a confident one approaches 0. Note the argmax is taken on the **logits**, so it never changes with temperature — only the confidence attached to it does.
